correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication produces B_theta=R*R=D+ts(exp(2i theta)W^2+exp(-2i theta)(W*)^2), with diagonal D. A trace word of length j can have nonzero Fourier exponent only if 2(a-b) is divisible by n. For 1<=j<k=n/gcd(n,2), no nonzero value of a-b is possible; at j=k only all-forward and all-backward words produce the frequency, with traces nQ^r and n conjugate(Q)^r. AM-GM for |w_j|^2 yields |Q|^r <=(H/n)^k, with exact equality iff all n moduli coincide when H>0; if any weight is zero all phase-sensitive closed walks vanish. Verified 24 independently generated weighted shifts across n=3...8 with zero-weight and complex-weight cases. The combinatorial divisibility argument is the unrestricted proof.

final_claim: For complex weighted n-cyclic shift W, n>=3, 0<t<1, R_theta=t exp(i theta)W+(1-t)exp(-i theta)W*: the first potentially theta-sensitive even Schatten exponent is 2n for n odd and n for n even; its moment is C+2n[t(1-t)]^k Re(exp(2ik theta) Q^r) where k=n/gcd(n,2), r=2k/n and Q=prod w_j. Oscillation is 4n[t(1-t)]^k |Q|^r and its sharp H-normalized bound is attained iff equal edge moduli.
